name: Milo
description: Milo is a partnership domino game played in Africa and parts of Indonesia. It uses the same equipment and basic play as Latin Partnership Dominoes, but with different scoring: the winning partnership gets one point for domino; if blocked, the partnership with the smallest total of pips on their tiles gets one point; if the tile that made domino causes both ends of the train to end in the same suit, the partnership scores two points (called a Milo). A game is five points.

rules.objective: Your partnership wins the game by being the first to reach five points. Points are scored for winning a round (domino or blocked round) and for a Milo (both ends of the train in the same suit when going out).
rules.gameplay: 1. First deal: the player with the double-six tile leads it. Later deals: turn to start passes right; starter may lead any tile. 2. Each player in turn adds a tile to the layout (same number to touching end). If unable to play, pass (e.g. knock). 3. Round ends when one player plays their last tile (domino) or all four pass (blocked). 4. Milo scoring: winning partnership gets one point for domino; blocked round won by partnership with smallest total pips (one point); if the tile that made domino leaves both ends of the train in the same suit, partnership scores two points (Milo). First partnership to five points wins the game.
keyRules: Tiles form a single line, end to end; doubles played at right angles. Same number must match at touching ends.
Must play if legally possible; otherwise pass.
Blocked round: team with lower pip total on unplayed tiles wins the round and scores one point.

scoring.description: Winning partnership scores one point for domino; one point for winning a blocked round (fewer pips); two points for a Milo (both ends same suit when going out). First to five points wins the game.
